report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Deadline fixed at 4 months and team composition known, but authentication/authorization scope and external service integration points (microservices, auth service, logging service) are not fully detailed, requiring adaptive refinement during Phase 2–3.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a centralized API gateway to manage microservices routing, authentication, rate limiting, and logging.
project_understanding.trigger: Multiple services with inconsistent APIs, security concerns, and lack of centralized rate limiting.
success_definition: All external APIs routed through gateway
Request logging for all API calls
supporting_quotes: Build an API gateway for our microservices.
Centralize API management with a unified gateway.
Multiple services with inconsistent APIs, security concerns, no centralized rate limiting.
All external APIs go through gateway. Consistent authentication across services. Request logging for all API calls.

assumption_log.what: Authentication service integration scope and SLA are defined and available; team has direct experience with the chosen auth mechanism (SSO, OAuth2, API keys, or mTLS).
assumption_log.why: Authentication is a hard dependency for gateway routing and security posture. If the auth service is unavailable, undocumented, or team lacks experience, architecture and timeline will require re-scoping.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Resource Planning) and Section 12.1 (Integration Management)
assumption_log.consequence: Gateway cannot enforce consistent authentication; team may need to build custom auth layer or delay launch pending auth service availability and documentation.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Assumes auth service is production-ready and team can integrate without custom development. Risks: If auth service is in-flight or team lacks experience, 2–4 week delay and potential re-architecture of gateway auth layer.

assumption_log.what: Microservice inventory, endpoint contracts, and current API inconsistencies are documented or discoverable; no undocumented legacy services will be discovered mid-project.
assumption_log.why: Gateway routing and versioning support depend on knowing which services exist and their current API signatures. Undiscovered services or breaking changes mid-project will expand scope.
assumption_log.consequence: Gateway routing rules incomplete at launch; post-launch service onboarding requires gateway reconfiguration and testing; timeline slips by 1–2 weeks per undiscovered service cluster.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Assumes all services are known and stable. Risks: If services are undocumented or rapidly evolving, gateway becomes a moving target and requires continuous re-scoping.

assumption_log.what: Data retention and audit logging requirements are standard (logs retained for 90 days, no PII redaction required); no HIPAA, SOC2, or regulatory data masking is mandated.
assumption_log.why: Logging architecture (storage, retention, encryption) is determined by compliance scope. If regulatory requirements exist, storage and pipeline design will differ significantly.
assumption_log.consequence: If regulatory requirements exist, logging pipeline must include encryption, PII redaction, and longer retention; storage costs and infrastructure complexity increase; 1–2 week delay for compliance design review.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Assumes standard internal audit logging with no regulatory masking. Risks: If compliance requirements exist, logging architecture must be re-designed and re-budgeted.

assumption_log.what: Load balancing is stateless round-robin or least-connections; no session affinity, sticky sessions, or stateful routing is required.
assumption_log.why: Load balancing complexity ranges from simple (round-robin) to complex (session affinity, circuit breakers, canary deployments). Stateless routing is the default for microservices gateways.
assumption_log.consequence: If stateful routing is required, gateway must implement session affinity and distributed state management; 1 week additional development and testing.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Assumes stateless load balancing, simplifying gateway logic and scaling. Risks: If services require session affinity, gateway becomes stateful and harder to scale horizontally.

hard.team_composition: 4 engineers (no roles, seniority, or stack experience specified)

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the team's experience with API gateway frameworks (Kong, AWS API Gateway, Envoy, Spring Cloud Gateway, etc.) and the chosen technology stack?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If team lacks experience with the chosen gateway platform, development velocity will be 30–50% slower; timeline may slip by 4–6 weeks.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is the authentication service (SSO, OAuth2, API keys, mTLS) already in production and documented, or will it be built/integrated as part of this project?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If auth service is not ready, gateway cannot enforce consistent authentication; project scope expands or launch is blocked.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: How many microservices must the gateway route to at launch, and what is the current state of their API documentation and versioning?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If service inventory is incomplete or APIs are undocumented, gateway routing rules will be incomplete; post-launch service onboarding will require continuous re-scoping.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions between rate limiting, versioning, and load balancing features?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Without a clear PO, feature prioritization will stall; team will build all features equally, risking timeline slip if scope must be cut.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Are there regulatory or compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) that mandate specific logging, encryption, or data retention policies?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If compliance requirements exist but are not discovered until Phase 2, logging architecture must be re-designed; 1–2 week delay and potential re-budgeting.
